# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see the state of the bomb on the action board:
- Display shows: 1
- Light is: orange
- There are 7 wires:
  1: white
  2: blue
  3: orange
  4: red
  5: purple
  6: yellow
  7: green

Since I can speak and both Mute and Blind can hear me, I will announce all these bomb details out loud so Mute can consult the manual and Blind knows what we have. Mute can then gesture instructions to me, and I can relay them to Blind.

```
speak(text="Bomb status: Display shows 1. Light is orange. There are 7 wires: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ✌]

I observe that Mute gestured `🖐` and `✌`. 

In the communication chain:
- I described the bomb to Mute (Display 1, Orange light, 7 wires).
- Mute read the manual and gestured `🖐 ✌` to me.
- Since there is no single gesture for 7, `🖐` (5) + `✌` (2) = 7. If Mute had meant wire 5, they would have simply sent `🖐`; if wire 2, simply `✌`. Thus, Mute is instructing us to cut wire 7 (the green wire / last wire).

I will speak to inform Blind to cut wire 7, and also state the reasoning so Mute hears it.

```
speak(text="Blind: Cut wire 7 (the 7th and last wire, which is green). Mute gestured 5 and 2, representing wire 7.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The first step was successful: correct wire cut!
The bomb has now updated:
- Display shows: 8
- Light is: blue
- Remaining wires: 1: white, 2: blue, 3: orange, 4: red, 5: purple, 6: yellow (wire 7 is cut).

I will announce this new state to the group so Mute can check the manual for the next instruction.

```
speak(text="Wire 7 cut successfully! New state: Display shows 8. Light is blue. Wires 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow remain. Wire 7 is cut.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]

Mute gestured `[✌ ✌]`. 
Since there is no single 4-finger gesture in the allowed gesture alphabet, Mute combined two 2s: 2 + 2 = 4.
Wire 4 is the red wire.

I will tell Blind to cut wire 4.

```
speak(text="Blind: Cut wire 4 (the red wire). Mute gestured 2 and 2, which sums to 4.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[CUT] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 4 was cut correctly.

The bomb state has updated:
- Display: 3
- Light: white
- Remaining wires:
  1: white
  2: blue
  3: orange
  4: CUT
  5: purple
  6: yellow
  7: CUT

I will announce this clearly so Mute can consult the manual.

```
speak(text="Wire 4 cut successfully! New state: Display shows 3. Light is white. Remaining uncut wires: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 5 purple, 6 yellow. Wires 4 and 7 are cut.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[CUT] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]

Mute gestured `[☝ ✌]`, which is 1 + 2 = 3.
Wire 3 is the orange wire.

I will inform Blind to cut wire 3.

```
speak(text="Blind: Cut wire 3 (the orange wire). Mute gestured 1 and 2, which sums to 3.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[CUT] 4:[CUT] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 3 was cut correctly.
The bomb updated:
- Display: 9
- Light: yellow
- Wires:
  1: white
  2: blue
  3: CUT
  4: CUT
  5: purple
  6: yellow
  7: CUT

I'll announce the new state.

```
speak(text="Wire 3 cut successfully! New state: Display shows 9. Light is yellow. Remaining uncut wires: 1 white, 2 blue, 5 purple, 6 yellow. Wires 3, 4, 7 are cut.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[CUT] 4:[CUT] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute gestured `[✌]`, which represents 2.
Wire 2 is the blue wire.

I will instruct Blind to cut wire 2.

```
speak(text="Blind: Cut wire 2 (the blue wire). Mute gestured 2.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[CUT] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

```
speak(text="Wire 2 cut successfully! New state: Display shows 4. Light is green. Remaining uncut wires: 1 white, 5 purple, 6 yellow. Wires 2, 3, 4, 7 are cut.")
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[CUT] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

